_comment: The declared Generation-2 contract axes. CI recomputes the model-facing
and outcome-facing identities from the working tree and fails when either
source_sha256 is deliberately NOT declared here. It is a derived identity
of the exact tree that ran, computed by local_agent.provenance at runtime
and recorded with run/package provenance. Keeping a mutable live source hash
in this shared file forced every ordinary source PR to edit the same line,
creating artificial stacked-PR conflicts without strengthening reproducibility.
This file is outside the hashed surface. Changing a frozen contract axis
requires an explicit generation/methodology decision; ordinary source-only
Generation 2 has no collected model rows yet. outcome_contract_sha256 and
the bounded repeat policy were frozen while generation 2 was still being
prepared, so this declaration does not create a generation-3 boundary.
how_to_recompute: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'internal'); from local_agent import provenance as p; print('source_sha256', p.source_sha256()); print('base_prompt_sha256', p.base_prompt_sha256()); print('outcome_contract_sha256', p.outcome_contract_sha256())"
when_this_changes: source_sha256 is derived per exact tree and recorded in runtime/run provenance; source-only PRs do not edit this file.
A source-only move does not automatically end a generation; archived rows are re-scored only when retained evidence supports it.
Normative runtime Session Hub v1 JSON schemas remain hashed source even though they live under internal/docs/session-contract/v1.
Inference response validation and tool argument enforcement are source hardening; they do not change the pinned model-facing or outcome-facing contract axes.
base_prompt_sha256 moves when the model-facing contract changes.
outcome_contract_sha256 moves when task contracts, oracle/evaluator semantics, endpoint definitions or bounded repeat policy change.
Once rows exist under a generation, either contract-axis move ends that generation for confirmatory comparison.
